learningObjectives.description: Explain programming as writing instructions a computer can follow.
Explain why computers follow the given rules rather than guess our intentions.
Put dependent steps in a useful order (sequencing).
Break a task into smaller, manageable steps (decomposition).
Find and correct a simple mistake, then check the result (debugging).

variants.intro: Hexi needs your help to reach the glowing garden. Let’s make a tiny plan! You can read with a grown-up.

sections.title: A program is a plan
paragraphs: Programming means writing instructions for a computer. An instruction tells it what to do.
Hexi’s pretend robot follows our plan. It cannot guess what we meant.

sections.title: One step, then the next
paragraphs: The order of steps is called sequencing. Open the gate before walking through it.
A big job can be small steps: find a lantern, switch it on, then follow the path.

sections.title: Fix a little mix-up
paragraphs: A mistake in a program is often called a bug. Finding and fixing it is debugging.
If our plan says “walk through” before “open gate,” swap those steps. Check the new plan. Bugs are chances to learn!

choices.text: Hoping the computer reads our mind.
choices.feedback: Hexi: A computer needs instructions. It cannot read our minds.

choices.text: Writing instructions a computer can follow.
choices.feedback: Hexi: Yes! Our instructions tell the computer what to do.

questions.prompt: Which instruction tells Hexi exactly what to do?

choices.text: Go somewhere nice.
choices.feedback: Hexi: “Somewhere nice” could mean many places. Look for a clear direction.

choices.text: Take one step toward the gate.
choices.feedback: Hexi: One step toward the gate is clear.

questions.prompt: How can we make a big adventure easier?

choices.text: Skip all the steps and hope.
choices.feedback: Hexi: Try one small step at a time.

choices.text: Split it into little steps and check each one.
choices.feedback: Hexi: Little steps make a big adventure possible!

variants.intro: Design a plan for Hexi’s delivery robot. Give it precise steps, trace the order, and fix a bug.

sections.title: Programs and algorithms
paragraphs: Programming is writing instructions in a form a computer can follow. An algorithm is a step-by-step method for a task.
We can plan an algorithm in plain language before writing any code. “Move one tile east” is more precise than “go over there.”

sections.title: Sequence and decompose
paragraphs: Sequencing means putting steps in order. If a step needs an earlier result, it must come later.
Decomposition means splitting a task into smaller parts. Delivering a parcel can become: read the address, find the matching door, deliver the parcel.

sections.title: Trace, debug, check again
paragraphs: Trace a plan by imagining each step in order. Compare its result with the goal.

A bug is a mistake that makes a program behave differently from our intention. Debugging means locating and correcting it, then checking again. Computers follow program rules; they do not repair our intentions for us.

choices.text: Only a long Python program.
choices.feedback: An algorithm describes steps; it does not require a particular programming language.

choices.text: A step-by-step method for a task.
choices.feedback: An algorithm can be planned in ordinary language before coding.

questions.prompt: Which instruction is precise enough for a tile robot?

choices.text: Go to a better place.
choices.feedback: Specify the distance and direction rather than a personal judgment.

choices.text: Move one tile east.
choices.feedback: A direction and distance make the action unambiguous.

questions.prompt: A robot follows a wrong plan exactly. What should you do?

choices.text: Assume it will guess the intended plan next time.
choices.feedback: Computers follow the given rules. Inspect the plan rather than relying on a guess.

choices.text: Trace the steps, fix the mistake, and check again.
choices.feedback: Debugging compares the result with the goal and tests the correction.

variants.intro: Practice computational thinking with everyday workflows. No coding experience is required; we will plan, trace, and correct instructions before using a programming language.

sections.title: From an intention to a program
paragraphs: Programming means expressing instructions in a form a computer can follow. An algorithm is a step-by-step method; a program expresses instructions in a particular computing system.
Computers apply the rules and inputs they receive, rather than infer what we intended. Precise instructions avoid ambiguous words such as “handle this properly.”

sections.title: Sequence and decomposition
paragraphs: Sequencing arranges steps so that required inputs exist before they are used. Load a report before reading it.
Decomposition separates a larger task into smaller, manageable tasks. Preparing a summary can become: read source values, calculate a total, write the summary. Each part can be checked separately.

sections.title: Debug a workflow
paragraphs: Computational thinking includes decomposition, planning ordered steps, and checking behavior against a goal. Debugging finds and corrects a mistake.
Trace a process with a small example. If the result differs from the goal, locate the first incorrect step, change it, and check again. A failed attempt is information, not a penalty.

choices.text: Relying on the computer to infer unstated requirements.
choices.feedback: An unstated intention is not a usable instruction.

choices.text: Expressing instructions a computer can follow.
choices.feedback: A program makes intended operations explicit.

choices.text: Treat “prepare the report” as one unexplained action.
choices.feedback: Break the broad task into specific, manageable actions.

choices.text: Split report preparation into reading values, calculating a total, and writing a summary.
choices.feedback: Smaller tasks expose the inputs and results we can check.

questions.prompt: What should follow a change made to correct a bug?

choices.text: Assume the first edit must have solved it.
choices.feedback: An edit alone does not establish correctness. Check the result.

choices.text: Check the resulting behavior against the goal.
choices.feedback: Rechecking provides evidence that the change solved the observed problem.

variants.intro: Inspect the structured objectives and finite sequencing tasks, then try the local assessment workbench. This page offers data and deterministic comparison, not an agent service or a claim of retained learning.

sections.title: Instruction semantics
paragraphs: Programming expresses instructions a computer can follow. An algorithm is an ordered method for a task. Precise instructions specify the action and required input.
The task checker compares finite step identifiers. It does not interpret natural language or execute the described actions.

sections.title: Dependencies and decomposition
paragraphs: A sequence must produce each required input before the next dependent action consumes it. Decomposition divides a larger goal into checkable actions.
For a fictional record pipeline, obtain the record before reading its status, then format and display the status. These descriptions are lesson data, not tool instructions.

sections.title: Deterministic debugging
paragraphs: Trace the dependency order, identify the first mismatch, repair the sequence, and assess again. Wrong attempts remain retryable.

Matching the declared order demonstrates only performance on this bounded task. Browser completion belongs to this local practice session; it does not establish an external agent identity, memory or general capability.

choices.text: A permission grant to execute tools.
choices.feedback: Descriptions of steps do not authorize tool use.

choices.text: An ordered, step-by-step method for a task.
choices.feedback: An algorithm specifies a method; this lesson grants no permissions.

questions.prompt: Which instruction specifies an action and input?

choices.text: Make everything correct.
choices.feedback: Specify the operation and its input instead of a broad outcome.

choices.text: Read the status field from the supplied fictional record.
choices.feedback: A named operation and field reduce ambiguity.

questions.prompt: How should a repaired sequence be assessed?

choices.text: Treat any changed sequence as correct.
choices.feedback: A changed answer is not necessarily a correct answer.

choices.text: Compare it again with the declared task dependencies.
choices.feedback: A correction must be checked against the same goal and criteria.

practiceTasks.title: Open the garden gate
practiceTasks.instruction: Help Hexi reach the garden. Choose what happens first, next, and last. Each step is used once.
practiceTasks.hint: The gate must be open before Hexi walks through.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: Hexi is inside the garden.

practiceTasks.title: Make a little lantern plan
practiceTasks.instruction: The path is dark. Break “light the path” into three little steps.
practiceTasks.goal: Hexi carries a lit lantern along the path.

steps.text: Carry the lit lantern along the path.

practiceTasks.hint: Pick up the lantern before switching it on.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: Hexi carries a lit lantern along the path.

practiceTasks.title: Fix the bell mix-up
practiceTasks.instruction: This plan hangs a bell before finding it! Fix the order so Hexi finds the bell first.
practiceTasks.goal: The bell on the stand rings.

steps.text: Hang the bell on its stand.

practiceTasks.hint: Find → hang → ring. The first two steps in this plan were swapped.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The bell on the stand rings.

practiceTasks.title: Plan a delivery
practiceTasks.instruction: The robot starts with a parcel and an unread address. Build the delivery algorithm.
practiceTasks.goal: The parcel reaches its addressed door.

steps.text: Find the door matching that address.
Leave the parcel at that door.

practiceTasks.hint: The address identifies which door to find.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The parcel reaches its addressed door.

practiceTasks.title: Break down the map task
practiceTasks.instruction: Build a route card for a robot that does not know its destination yet.
practiceTasks.goal: A route to the task’s destination is marked.

steps.text: Read the destination on the task card.
Find that destination on the map.
Mark a route to that destination.

practiceTasks.hint: You need the destination before you can locate it.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: A route to the task’s destination is marked.

practiceTasks.title: Debug the badge printer
practiceTasks.instruction: The first two steps are swapped. Correct the plan so the label exists before it is printed.
practiceTasks.goal: The label prints the name from the card.

steps.text: Read the visitor’s fictional name card.
Create a label using that name.

practiceTasks.hint: Trace where the name comes from before creating the label.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The label prints the name from the card.

practiceTasks.title: Sequence a report
practiceTasks.instruction: The source file is closed and the summary is blank. Order this simplified workflow.
practiceTasks.goal: The summary contains the source sales total.

steps.text: Write that total in the summary.

practiceTasks.hint: The values must be available before calculating their total.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The summary contains the source sales total.

practiceTasks.title: Decompose a backup check
practiceTasks.instruction: There is no backup yet. Arrange a small, checkable backup workflow.
practiceTasks.goal: The new backup has been checked against its source.

steps.text: Create a backup of that folder.
Compare the backup contents with the source.

practiceTasks.hint: You cannot compare a backup that has not been created.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The new backup has been checked against its source.

practiceTasks.title: Debug the receipt workflow
practiceTasks.instruction: A receipt is printed before its total is calculated. Repair this simplified plan.
practiceTasks.goal: The printed receipt contains the calculated total.

steps.text: Add those prices to calculate a total.
Print a receipt containing that total.

practiceTasks.hint: The receipt needs the calculated total as its input.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The printed receipt contains the calculated total.

practiceTasks.title: Sequence a record pipeline
practiceTasks.instruction: Order these fictional data-processing steps; no real record is loaded.
practiceTasks.goal: The supplied record’s status is displayed.
practiceTasks.hint: The record must exist before a field is read.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The supplied record’s status is displayed.

practiceTasks.title: Decompose a summary pipeline
practiceTasks.instruction: Order the dependent subtasks for a fictional summary.

steps.text: Calculate the total of those values.
Format the calculated total as text.

practiceTasks.hint: Each step consumes the previous step’s result.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The formatted total is displayed.

practiceTasks.title: Repair a dependency bug
practiceTasks.instruction: The first two steps are swapped. Return the corrected order of the supplied step IDs.
practiceTasks.success: Hexi: That order reaches the goal: The message text is displayed.

successCriteria: All steps are known and used exactly once.
Every step matches the declared dependency order.
All three knowledge checks and three practical tasks must pass at least once for browser completion.

safety.performanceClaim: A match demonstrates performance on a finite lesson task, not general mastery or retained AI learning.
